memory_leak_candidates.issue: ItemComponent.mounted() attaches an anonymous 'wizard:add-to-cart' listener to this.$refs.itemVariationModal. The handler reference is NOT stored, so beforeUnmount() at line 1495 cannot remove it. The document-level 'click' handler IS properly removed via stored this._posTileClickHandler, but the modal handler is unrecoverable.
memory_leak_candidates.impact: Modal is a child DOM node of ItemComponent — Vue 3 unmount removes the modal node from DOM. Once detached, the listener becomes GC-eligible with the node. So in practice, no listener accumulates across remounts: the leak is bounded to the lifetime of the modal element. Risk = effectively nil for cashier-8h scenario (single POS mount, modal opens/closes but listener stays on same DOM node).
memory_leak_candidates.remediation_proposed: Store handler in this._wizardSubmitHandler = (...) => {...}; modal.addEventListener('wizard:add-to-cart', this._wizardSubmitHandler); remove in beforeUnmount() with modal.removeEventListener(). Pure-hygiene fix, not blocking.

memory_leak_candidates.issue: Two helpers attach anonymous document-level click listeners. Handler refs not stored — never removable. If called multiple times, listeners accumulate on document.
memory_leak_candidates.impact: VERIFIED DEAD CODE — grep -rn 'singleSlideDown|singleGroupActive' yields ONLY the definitions in appService.js (no callers anywhere in the codebase). Functions are never invoked. Zero runtime impact.
memory_leak_candidates.remediation_proposed: Delete dead code OR refactor to store/remove handlers. Defer to V1.0.2 cleanup wave.

memory_leak_candidates.issue: Both MapComponent files attach an anonymous click listener to a DOM element looked up by getElementById('map-current-location'). No corresponding removeEventListener, no beforeUnmount hook in the component at all.
memory_leak_candidates.impact: currentLocationButton is part of the MapComponent's own template DOM subtree — Vue removes it on unmount. Listener is GC'd with the detached node. Practical leak = none in a typical mount/unmount cycle. Worst case: if the same MapComponent is mounted and the listener is bound twice without an intermediate DOM rebuild, you'd see double-fire — not a memory leak.
memory_leak_candidates.remediation_proposed: Add beforeUnmount() with explicit removeEventListener + handler stored on instance. Defensive cleanup, not a memory bug.

Also run `getEventListeners(document).click.length` in DevTools — expect bounded count (≤2: the document-level posTileClickHandler from ItemComponent's mounted hook, properly removed). verdict_justification: Zero P0/P1 leaks identified in cashier-relevant POS surface (PosComponent, PaymentComponent, ItemComponent, PosOrdersTrackerComponent, FloorplanComponent).

All 9 setInterval timers in PosComponent (kiosk poll, shortcuts refresh, cart bump, total flash, success flash, availability toast, offline flush, delivery autocomplete, etc.) cleared symmetrically in beforeUnmount.
All Echo subscriptions go through the canonical onEvents() helper which returns unsubscribe(); every consumer calls it.
All wsService.on() bindings have matching .off() in _unbindWsService.
Late-callback safety via _destroyed flag introduced 2026-05-20 (WT-R1-F2) prevents reactive-state mutations on torn-down instances.
No Vuex module observed accumulating realtime event payloads without TTL or replace semantics. kdsInflight specifically designed with 10-min lazy purge.
3 minor hygiene findings (1 ItemComponent modal anonymous listener, 1 dead-code in appService.js, 1 MapComponent click handler) — all bounded to component DOM lifetime, no session-long accumulation.

Conclusion: POS layer is structurally robust for an 8h cashier shift. Expected behavior: single POS mount at login, never unmounted during shift → setInterval timers fire steadily, Echo channel subscribed once. Memory profile should be FLAT (modulo cart payload churn cleared on submit).
